claim_verdicts.evidence: "For a Pod that defines an `emptyDir` volume, the volume is created when the Pod is assigned to a node. As the name says, the `emptyDir` volume is initially empty. ... When a Pod is removed from a node for any reason, the data in the `emptyDir` is deleted permanently." Note: "A container crashing does *not* remove a Pod from a node. The data in an `emptyDir` volume is safe across container crashes."

git show stage-3:deploy/k8s/db.yaml (via tools/extract-code): Deployment `db`, `replicas: 1`, `image: postgres:17.6-alpine`, volumeMount `data` at `/var/lib/postgresql/data`, volume `- name: data` / `emptyDir: {}`.

"A _PersistentVolume_ (PV) is a piece of storage in the cluster ... PVs are volume plugins like Volumes, but have a lifecycle independent of any individual Pod that uses the PV." "A _PersistentVolumeClaim_ (PVC) is a request for storage by a user. ... Claims can request specific size and access modes". Namespaces page: "low-level resources, such as Nodes and PersistentVolumes, are not in any namespace." PVCs: "PersistentVolumeClaims are namespaced objects".

"A control loop in the control plane watches for new PVCs, finds a matching PV (if possible), and binds them together. ... the user will always get at least what they asked for, but the volume may be in excess of what was requested. Once bound, PersistentVolumeClaim binds are exclusive, regardless of how they were bound. A PVC to PV binding is a one-to-one mapping". pvc.txt line 7: `data   Bound    100Mi      ReadWriteOnce`.

"`ReadWriteOnce`: the volume can be mounted as read-write by a single node. ReadWriteOnce access mode still can allow multiple pods to access (read from or write to) that volume when the pods are running on the same node." pvc.txt lines 24-30: both lines in note.txt, writer and writer-2 Running, `nodes they run on: 1`.

"Pods access storage by using the claim as a volume. Claims must exist in the same namespace as the Pod using the claim. The cluster finds the claim in the Pod's namespace and uses it to get the PersistentVolume backing the claim." "Users ... access their claimed PVs by including a `persistentVolumeClaim` section in a Pod's `volumes` block." Example uses `persistentVolumeClaim: claimName: myclaim`. data-writer-pod.yaml lines 18-21 match.

Round 2: kubelet removed. Claim now matches docs: "Pods access storage by using the claim as a volume. ... The volume is then mounted to the host and into the Pod." data-writer-pod.yaml lines 15-17 mount `data` at `/data`; lesson section 4 now reads "On the Pod's node, the volume is mounted into the container at `/data`".

PVs "have a lifecycle independent of any individual Pod that uses the PV." Execution: pvc.txt lines 10-14 `pod "writer" deleted ...` then `data   Bound`; lines 16-19 new `writer` prints `order 13: written by writer`.

tools/extract-code data-pvc.yaml --tag stage-3: `kind: PersistentVolumeClaim`, `name: data`, `namespace: storage-lessons`, `accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]`, `storage: 100Mi`. data-writer-pod.yaml lines 15-21 mount `data` at `/data`, line 14 `command: ["sleep", "3600"]`.

"Currently when a Pod is created, its hostname (as observed from within the Pod) is the Pod's `metadata.name` value." data-writer-pod.yaml sets no spec.hostname. pvc.txt lines 19, 24-25: `written by writer`, `written by writer-2`.

"`nodeName` is a more direct form of node selection than affinity or `nodeSelector`. ... If the `nodeName` field is not empty, the scheduler ignores the Pod and the kubelet on the named node tries to place the Pod on that node."
